title: Natural clopen descent through the connected-component quotient
statement: Use the universe conventions of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X,Y$ be arbitrary topological spaces and $f:X\to Y$ a continuous map. For each topological space $Z$, write $\operatorname{Clop}(Z)$ for its open and closed subsets and let $\pi_0(Z)$ be its set of connected components (maximal connected subsets), with the quotient topology for the surjection $q_Z:Z\to\pi_0(Z)$ sending a point to its component. There is a unique continuous map $h:\pi_0(X)\to\pi_0(Y)$ satisfying $h q_X=q_Y f$, and it sends the component of $x$ to the component of $f(x)$. For every $Z$, inverse image $\beta_Z:\operatorname{Clop}(\pi_0(Z))\to\operatorname{Clop}(Z)$ along $q_Z$ is bijective; its inverse sends $U$ to $q_Z(U)$, which is clopen and satisfies $q_Z^{-1}(q_Z(U))=U$. For every clopen $V\subseteq\pi_0(Y)$ one has $\beta_X(h^{-1}(V))=f^{-1}(\beta_Y(V))$. Consequently $f^{-1}:\operatorname{Clop}(Y)\to\operatorname{Clop}(X)$ is bijective if and only if $h^{-1}:\operatorname{Clop}(\pi_0(Y))\to\operatorname{Clop}(\pi_0(X))$ is bijective. No compactness, separation, or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Agent component-quotient functoriality and natural clopen descent, expanding the clopen-saturation passage in Tag 0900 (lemma-pi0-profinite), proof. This statement does not claim the profiniteness conclusion of that tag.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-connected-component-maximality], $C_x$ is connected, contains $x$, and contains every connected subset through $x$. If $y\in C_x$, maximality at $y$ gives $C_x\subseteq C_y$; hence $x\in C_y$ and maximality at $x$ gives the reverse inclusion. Thus these sets partition $X$ into precisely its maximal connected subsets. This justifies the point-component surjection $q_X$, and likewise for any other space. The Lean proof uses Mathlib's existing ConnectedComponents quotient rather than reconstructing this partition.

For a component $C_x$, the image $f(C_x)$ is connected: it contains $f(x)$, and the inverse images of a relatively clopen partition of $f(C_x)$ form such a partition of $C_x$; one part is empty, and surjectivity onto the image makes its corresponding image part empty. This uses exactly [def-weil-connected-scheme]. By [lem-sfb-connected-component-maximality], $f(C_x)\subseteq C_{f(x)}$. Consequently $q_X(x)=q_X(x\prime)$ implies $q_Y(f(x))=q_Y(f(x\prime))$. The rule $h(q_X(x))=q_Y(f(x))$ is well defined. Surjectivity of $q_X$ proves its uniqueness and $h q_X=q_Y f$. In Lean choose Continuous.connectedComponentsMap; its value on mk is definitionally mk (f x). The uniqueness proof uses ContinuousMap.ext, surjective_coe and congrFun on the normalization equality.

source.place: Tag 0376 (lemma-image-connected-space), proof; Tag 004T (lemma-connected-components), maximality. Agent quotient construction.

proof.text: For open $W\subseteq\pi_0(Y)$, the quotient topology makes $q_Y^{-1}(W)$ open. Hence $q_X^{-1}(h^{-1}(W))=f^{-1}(q_Y^{-1}(W))$ is open by continuity of $f$. The defining quotient topology on $\pi_0(X)$ then makes $h^{-1}(W)$ open. Thus $h$ is continuous; this argument also shows that each $q_Z$ is continuous. Lean uses Continuous.connectedComponentsMap_continuous and ConnectedComponents.continuous_coe, which already implement this quotient-topology argument.

source.place: Tag 08ZL (lemma-space-connected-components), quotient-topology construction; agent open-preimage calculation.

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq Z$ be clopen and $x\in U$. By [lem-sfb-connected-component-maximality], $C_x$ is connected and contains $x$. The relatively clopen partition $C_x=(C_x\cap U)\amalg(C_x\setminus U)$ has nonempty first part, so [def-weil-connected-scheme] forces $C_x\subseteq U$. Thus $U$ is a union of whole components, and $q_Z^{-1}(q_Z(U))=U$. The private helper clopen_descent_aux obtains this identity by rewriting connectedComponents_preimage_image and IsClopen.biUnion_connectedComponent_eq, the existing Mathlib saturation proof based on the component maximality and connectedness above.

source.place: Tag 0900 (lemma-pi0-profinite), proof sentence beginning “Since U_alpha is open and closed”; only the saturation argument is used.

proof.text: Put $A=q_Z(U)$. The preceding equality and the quotient topology show $A$ open. Also $q_Z^{-1}(\pi_0(Z)\setminus A)=Z\setminus U$ is open, so its quotient counterpart is open; hence $A$ is clopen. Continuity of $q_Z$ sends clopens to clopens by inverse image, since complements commute with inverse image. The identities $q_Z^{-1}(q_Z(U))=U$ and $q_Z(q_Z^{-1}(V))=V$ for all $V\subseteq\pi_0(Z)$ (surjectivity) exhibit $\beta_Z$ and $U\mapsto q_Z(U)$ as mutual inverses. Apply ConnectedComponents.isQuotientMap_coe.isClopen_preimage to the saturation identity. Injectivity of beta follows from Set.preimage_injective and surjective_coe; its surjectivity has the explicit witness q_Z(U). Both parts are proved in clopen_descent_aux.

source.place: Tag 0900 (lemma-pi0-profinite), same saturation sentence; agent quotient-topology and set-image expansion.

proof.text: For clopen $V\subseteq\pi_0(Y)$ and $x\in X$, membership in $\beta_X(h^{-1}(V))$ means $h(q_X(x))\in V$, equivalently $q_Y(f(x))\in V$, equivalently $x\in f^{-1}(\beta_Y(V))$. This proves the claimed equality. All four inverse-image maps have clopen values because their maps are continuous. The chosen Mathlib component map makes the Lean carrier equality definitional, so rfl proves naturality.

source.place: Agent naturality calculation from the normalization, expanding the component-quotient comparison following Tag 0900.

proof.text: The equality gives $f^{-1}=\beta_X\circ h^{-1}\circ\beta_Y^{-1}$ and $h^{-1}=\beta_X^{-1}\circ f^{-1}\circ\beta_Y$ on clopens. Composition with mutually inverse bijections preserves and reflects injectivity and surjectivity, proving the final equivalence. No step selects a point unless one has already been given; for the empty space both clopen sets consist of the empty subset, so all assertions remain valid. In Lean name the four clopen functions F, H, beta_X and beta_Y. The square F composed with beta_Y = beta_X composed with H is rfl. Function.Bijective.of_comp_iff cancels the bijective beta_Y, and Function.Bijective.of_comp_iff' cancels beta_X. The helper is universe-polymorphic and therefore applies separately to X, Y and the quantified space Z.

source.place: Agent set-theoretic conjugacy consequence of the preceding naturality equality.

lean.statement: theorem clopen_descent_naturality {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : X → Y) (hf : Continuous f) : ∃ h : ContinuousMap (ConnectedComponents X) (ConnectedComponents Y), (h ∘ (mk : X → ConnectedComponents X) = (mk : Y → ConnectedComponents Y) ∘ f) ∧ (∀ g : ContinuousMap (ConnectedComponents X) (ConnectedComponents Y), g ∘ (mk : X → ConnectedComponents X) = (mk : Y → ConnectedComponents Y) ∘ f → g = h) ∧ (∀ x : X, h (mk x) = mk (f x)) ∧ (∀ (Z : Type w) [TopologicalSpace Z], Function.Bijective (fun V : TopologicalSpace.Clopens (ConnectedComponents Z) ↦ (⟨mk ⁻¹' (V : Set (ConnectedComponents Z)), V.isClopen.preimage continuous_coe⟩ : TopologicalSpace.Clopens Z)) ∧ ∀ U : TopologicalSpace.Clopens Z, IsClopen ((mk : Z → ConnectedComponents Z) '' (U : Set Z)) ∧ (mk : Z → ConnectedComponents Z) ⁻¹' ((mk : Z → ConnectedComponents Z) '' (U : Set Z)) = (U : Set Z)) ∧ (∀ V : TopologicalSpace.Clopens (ConnectedComponents Y), (mk : X → ConnectedComponents X) ⁻¹' (h ⁻¹' (V : Set (ConnectedComponents Y))) = f ⁻¹' ((mk : Y → ConnectedComponents Y) ⁻¹' (V : Set (ConnectedComponents Y)))) ∧ (Function.Bijective (fun U : TopologicalSpace.Clopens Y ↦ (⟨f ⁻¹' (U : Set Y), U.isClopen.preimage hf⟩ : TopologicalSpace.Clopens X)) ↔ Function.Bijective (fun V : TopologicalSpace.Clopens (ConnectedComponents Y) ↦ (⟨h ⁻¹' (V : Set (ConnectedComponents Y)), V.isClopen.preimage h.continuous⟩ : TopologicalSpace.Clopens (ConnectedComponents X))))
